claim: Defence cost and system performance overhead are defender-side efficiency metrics of MTD, with Mendonça et al. as an example.
quote: The proposed models focus on analyzing relevant performance metrics, such as response time, throughput, service utilization, the number of blocked and dropped jobs, job completion probability, and cost of services deployed in SDNs under deployment versus nondeployment of MTD techniques.
issue: Survives the adversarial read: performance degradation and cost under a time-based MTD are the paper's subject.

claim: Quality of service is a defender-side efficiency metric of MTD, with Mendonça et al. as an example.
quote: In addition, we demonstrate the effect of triggering a time-based MTD operation on performance degradation (e.g., jobs dropped or response time) and quality-of-service (QoS) of the system.
locator: p. 41 printed (PDF p. 1), abstract; the body measures the same quantities (response time, throughput, job completion probability) without the term 'QoS'
issue: The term 'quality of service' appears only in the abstract; the body's measures are QoS measures, so the cell holds, but a quote from the body cannot name it.

claim: Stochastic Petri nets are an established formalism in MTD evaluation (Mendonça et al. use one).
quote: This paper adopts an extension of Petri nets called deterministic and stochastic Petri net (DSPN)21 for evaluating services with or without an MTD mechanism deployed in SDN environments.
issue: One instance, and of a DSPN (deterministic and exponential timed transitions) evaluating MTD's performance cost, not its security. The source says Petri nets 'have been widely used for evaluating the dependability and performance of IT systems', not that they are established in MTD evaluation. Supports 'have been used to evaluate MTD'.
fix_text: "are an established formalism in MTD evaluation" -> "have been used to evaluate MTD" (same fix as chobenasher2018 on this unit).

claim: Other models that time attack steps set their durations by judgement where data are missing.
quote: The input parameters marked with ? were reasonably estimated, as they were not found in the literature or product specifications.
locator: p. 48 printed (PDF p. 8), Sec. 4.1; the ?-marked parameters in Table 4, p. 50 printed (PDF p. 10), are the mean time to update vIPs and the profit per short and long job
issue: Mendonça et al. do estimate parameters where data are missing, but their model times jobs, switches and MTD operations; it times no attack step (no attacker transition is parameterised). Cited as an example of 'models that time attack steps', it is about a different system.
fix_text: Drop mendonca2023 from this sentence (mcqueen2006 carries it), or widen the clause: "as other models that time attack steps do where data are missing" -> "as other timed models do for parameters without data".
